name: Detroit techno
blurb: Machine drums under strings and bell tones that sound like the future.

sounds.name: FM bell
sounds.why: One sine wave bending the pitch of another very fast. The result is glassy and metallic, like a bell that was never struck.

ingredients.name: Add FM
ingredients.adds: A second, unheard sine wobbles the pitch of the first hundreds of times a second.
ingredients.listenFor: New, clangy overtones appear that are not in any normal waveform.

ingredients.name: Let the shimmer fade
ingredients.adds: The FM is strong at the start of the note and dies away.
ingredients.listenFor: A bright "ting", then a pure tone.

knobs.label: FM decay
knobs.above: It stays metallic all the way through.

ingredients.name: Ring out
ingredients.adds: The note fades like a struck bell.

knobs.above: Notes pile on top of each other.

ingredients.name: Echo
ingredients.adds: Repeats that fill the gaps in the melody.

sounds.why: The same 909 as house, but drier and harder, with nothing soft around it.
Hats and a ride cymbal straight from the 909. The ride on the offbeat is the sound of a Detroit track picking up speed.
A plain low tone that stays out of the way. The bass supports; the strings and bells are the stars.
Cold, slow string chords over hard drums. That contrast, machine below and emotion above, is the Detroit sound.

sounds.name: Delayed chord stab
sounds.why: A single minor seventh stab fed into a long echo, so two hits fill the whole bar.
